title: One Point Lesson - Corrosion / Thickness Inspection (OPL-FA-8901-06)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-FA-8901-06 - Corrosion / Thickness Inspection.

Equipment: FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM), Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 8900 - HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-8901 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-8901.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains corrosion / thickness inspection for FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM) in the HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM. The boot and shell bottom see the water phase and are corrosion-prone; periodic thickness checks catch wall loss early. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Take UT thickness readings on the shell bottom and boot
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Compare readings to the 3.0 mm corrosion allowance
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Inspect the mist pad and vortex breaker at turnaround
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Record the readings in the RBI / inspection file
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Flag any accelerated wall loss to inspection engineering
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Statutory relief valve test | Likely Cause: Set pressure drift found | Action: Overhauled PSV-8901, lapped seat, re-set 10 barg, certified
- Symptom: Boot drain valve N4 passing / leaking | Likely Cause: Seat eroded by water/solids | Action: Reseated / replaced boot drain valve HV-8904
- Symptom: Scheduled corrosion monitoring of boot | Likely Cause: Wall thickness within corrosion allowance | Action: UT survey of boot and shell bottom, logged in RBI file

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The boot and shell bottom see the water phase and are corrosion-prone; periodic thickness checks catch wall loss early.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-8901: e.g. LSHH-8901 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-8901 before working on FA-8901.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
